titre: Enrolling my child in preschool or elementary school
resume: Two steps: the town hall (mairie) issues an enrollment certificate, then the school admits the child. The exact list of documents to bring, and what changes when the parents are separated.
aQuoiCaSert: Education is compulsory from age 3 to 16. For a first enrollment in a public preschool (école maternelle) or elementary school (école élémentaire), you first go to the school affairs department of the town hall (mairie), which gives you an enrollment certificate stating the assigned school. Then the school's principal admits your child on presentation of this certificate and proof of vaccinations. Preparing the documents in advance saves you a second trip.
quiEstConcerne: Parents of a child who turns 3 in the calendar year of the start of the school year.
Parents who are moving or changing their child's school.
Families who have just arrived in Guadeloupe, including with a child who does not yet speak French.
aSavoir: The child must be enrolled in preschool at the start of the school year in the calendar year they turn 3. Public school is free.
Enrollment at the town hall must be done by June at the latest before the school year starts. Enrollment usually opens in March, sometimes earlier depending on the town.

The town hall accepts as ID the family record book (livret de famille), ID card, passport or a copy of a birth certificate extract. A sworn statement (attestation sur l'honneur) may be accepted for both identity and address.
As a rule, children are enrolled in the school of the catchment area set by the town. Another school requires an exemption (dérogation), which is not automatic.

Separated parents: enrolling in or withdrawing from a public school is a routine decision. One parent can do it alone and is presumed to have the other's consent, but must inform them. If the other parent tells the school they disagree, the school must take this into account. In case of disagreement, the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF) can decide.
Sole parental authority: if a judgment gives it to only one parent, that parent decides alone. Bring a copy of the judgment so the school and the town hall take it into account.

Changing schools during the school career: the new school usually asks for the certificat de radiation (certificat de radiation from the school roll) issued by the former school, in addition to the town hall's enrollment certificate.

documents.libelle: The child's family record book, ID card, passport or copy of birth certificate extract
documents.detail: Original to present. No birth certificate? Request it free of charge online on service-public.gouv.fr or at the town hall of the place of birth.

documents.libelle: ID of the parent doing the enrollment
documents.detail: Original. ID card, passport or residence permit.
Utility bill, rent receipt or tax notice. Living with someone? Bring a letter of accommodation from your host, with their ID and their own proof of address. A sworn statement may be accepted.

documents.libelle: Health record book (carnet de santé, vaccination pages) or certificate of contraindication
documents.detail: Original to show; a photocopy of the vaccination pages is often requested.

documents.libelle: Judgment or agreement setting parental authority and residence, if you are separated
documents.detail: Copy. Essential in case of sole parental authority or if residence is set with one parent.

documents.libelle: Certificat de radiation from the former school
documents.detail: Only when changing schools. Ask the former school's principal for it.

documents.libelle: Enrollment certificate issued by the town hall
documents.detail: Original to hand to the school's principal. Keep a photo or a copy.

etapes.titre: Contact your town hall's school affairs department
etapes.detail: Ask for the enrollment dates, whether you need an appointment, whether there is an online service, and the exact list of documents: it varies from one town to another.

The child's ID (or livret de famille), your ID, recent proof of address (or letter of accommodation), up-to-date health record book, judgment if you are separated, certificat de radiation if changing schools. Bring photocopies.

etapes.titre: Submit the file at the town hall and collect the enrollment certificate
etapes.detail: The certificate states the school your child is assigned to. Ask for an exemption at this point if you want another school.

etapes.titre: Have your child admitted to the school
etapes.detail: Present the enrollment certificate and proof of vaccinations to the school's principal. Give both parents' contact details and the list of people allowed to pick up the child.
If you are separated, let the other parent know about the enrollment, preferably in writing (text message or email).
The enrollment is valid for the whole of preschool. Moving up to CP (first grade) happens automatically if the town has an elementary school.

ou.detail: Support center for newly arrived pupils: online enrollment file for those under 17 years and 5 months. Head office in Les Abymes, local office in Marigot (Saint-Martin). Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 12 p.m.
